coverage: Five stories · one concept · one question

cards.headline: Should an app know your age?
cards.summary: Microsoft introduced tools that let Windows apps request an age range without receiving your full birth date. The tools are available to Windows Insider testers; a wider release is still coming.
cards.whyItMatters: An app could change which features you can use based on your age group. Sharing less information can protect privacy, but the rules still deserve scrutiny.

csp.connection: Design choices affect privacy, access, and who gets to use a feature.

cards.headline: A faster start to a secure connection
cards.summary: Cloudflare announced an update that checks which encryption methods a website’s server supports before connecting. It prefers protection against future quantum attacks when the server supports it, and reports fewer connection retries during rollout.
cards.whyItMatters: Security depends on the connections between servers as well as your browser. Choosing a compatible method in advance can make a secure connection faster.

csp.connection: Protocols let different computers agree on how to communicate securely.

cards.headline: How do you know a new feature is better?
cards.summary: Spotify’s engineers published an explanation of how they evaluate A/B tests, experiments comparing two versions of a feature. They argue that rules for collecting and interpreting evidence matter more than choosing a fashionable statistical method.
cards.whyItMatters: More clicks do not automatically prove a redesign works. When you test your own project, decide what success means before looking at the results.

csp.connection: The way data is collected and analyzed shapes the conclusions we draw.

cards.headline: AI coding tools reach isolated company networks
cards.summary: GitHub’s new Enterprise Server release lets administrators configure its AI coding assistant for environments disconnected from GitHub Cloud. This feature is a technical preview and requires a configured model provider.
cards.whyItMatters: Some organizations cannot send their code to a public cloud service. Where an AI tool runs matters alongside what it can do.

csp.connection: Network design controls which systems can communicate and where data travels.

cards.headline: Security updates are part of owning software
cards.summary: Canada’s Cyber Centre issued an advisory about September security updates for Microsoft products. It recommends applying the relevant updates after reviewing Microsoft’s guidance.
cards.whyItMatters: A program can work normally and still contain a security flaw. Keeping your personal devices updated helps close known weaknesses; school-managed devices follow school procedures.

cards.headline: An age range can be enough information
cards.summary: Suppose a feature needs to know whether a user is at least 18. It may only need a yes-or-no answer, rather than a birth date. An abstraction keeps the information needed for a task while hiding other detail.
cards.whyItMatters: When you design an app, ask what information it actually needs. Collecting less personal data gives you less sensitive information to protect.

csp.connection: Abstraction exposes useful information while hiding unnecessary detail.

cards.headline: Who should decide what an app lets a teenager do?
cards.summary: Consider the student, their family, the app’s designer, and the school. Choose one feature where age should matter and one where it should not. What information would you need to defend your choices?
